rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card and dated predictions before any outcome fit, synthetic validation first (it rescaled planted effects and showed that the direction test is blind for idle-read classes, amendment A1), replication on G51, G38, G04, three native tests (NE43, G05 dose, NE38), 70 per-period estimate rows, confirmatory script frozen and dry-run, not run. Analysis limited to 3+1 periods by the compute budget.
rationale.faithfulness: The claim as posed is refuted: leave-one-class-out loses to class-specific fits in all four periods (T 0.0-0.75), and the shared direction fails in G38 and G04. Only a narrower, post hoc regularity holds (shared response at the read-out call, 77-100% in G51 and for G04 humans), plus NE43 invariance and saturating dose. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E1 F1 G1 H1 I0; no holdout.
rationale.usefulness: Gives an operator a compact, measured description of the immediate effect of any input at the call that reads it (kappa, h, d per class; the nudge and the @-mention look alike there), shows the read-out delay alone is not enough for message classes, and locates the class differences in the aftermath (nudge tails, regime-I edge catalysis). The NE43 invariance and the G05 'one read = one kick' are directly usable.

one_line: One triple per operator-input class does not predict a held-out class (G51 transfer 0.47–0.72); classes share only the read-out-call response and differ in tails.

models.note: One field-catalyst triple per class fails leave-one-class-out
Shared call-clock kernel holds at read-out, not in tails

v2.claim: No single (field, catalysis, read-out delay) triple transfers across operator input classes (leave-one-class-out fails in G51, G38, G04, G05); at the read-out all classes act as a talk-ward field with small catalysis, and class differences live in the tails
v2.scope: G51, G38, G04 (replication); natives G05, NE43, NE38

penalty: read-out-only regularity is post hoc
